summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted after a mechanical fall while walking, resulting in soft tissue injuries to her right knee and left elbow, with no fractures on imaging. She reported pain in the left arm and nosebleed from impact, but no loss of consciousness. Initial evaluation revealed hypotension, prompting temporary discontinuation of antihypertensives and diuretics. Her blood pressure stabilized, and she was restarted on half-dose furosemide while holding bumetanide and other cardiac medications. Chronic thrombocytopenia led to discontinuation of aspirin and avoidance of NSAIDs. Pain improved with acetaminophen, and she was discharged home with a sling, TED hose, and visiting physical therapy. Outpatient follow-up was advised for medication reconciliation, stool changes, and evaluation of a stable but loosening cervical screw and a slightly enlarged retropharyngeal mass.
